proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the effective admission lag varies over time (e.g., early vs late season), a fixed 2-week delay can cause phase errors and rolling-split sensitivity around the peak.
proposals.rationale: Anchor specification matching prior best: SEIRS captures waning immunity/reinfection dynamics while delayed_I with a 2-week lag aligns the latent infectious proxy to observed hospitalization-rate timing; expected to be robust for moderate peakiness and high rate scale.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-lagging can shift the predicted peak too late and smear the rise, degrading fit when the true lag is closer to ~2 weeks.
proposals.rationale: Neighborhood exploration around the anchor to hedge delay sensitivity: a 3-week lag may better match slower hospitalization timing in some splits while retaining the same SEIRS reinfection flexibility.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in a short series; I+H can blur interpretability and still misalign timing if the effective lag is strongly ~2–3 weeks, leading to biased peak timing or amplitude.
proposals.rationale: Introduce an explicit hospitalization compartment while avoiding pure instantaneous H-only observation: observing I+H can act as a mild smoothing/aggregation that partially absorbs timing mismatch and may improve robustness without requiring a separate delay parameter in the DSL.
